source_text: Verum quia eiusdem quam supra exposuerat quaestionis incurrebat occasio, ut opponeretur videlicet liberatos a lege, quae intendebat iram, securos posse sub gratiae Dei benignitate peccare, subdidit protinus: Quid ergo? Peccabimus, quoniam non sumus sub lege, sed sub gratia? Absit! An ignoratis, quoniam cui exhibetis vos servos ad oboediendum, servi estis eius, cui oboedistis, sive peccati sive oboeditionis iustitiae? [n391] Iamne ei credimus, de cuius disseruerit hactenus conditione peccati? Cui, inquit, exhibetis vos servos ad oboediendum, eius servi estis, sive peccati, sive iustitiae. Ubi hic ergo indicatur ab Apostolo peccatum illud, quod ante voluntatis tempora, ante oboedientium studium, ante scientiae et conscientiae aetatem ipsis fingitur supervolasse seminibus? Quod certe nisi in Manichaeorum libris inveniri non potest.
pass_a_gloss: But because an occasion of the same question which he had explained above was occurring, so that namely it would be objected that those freed from the law, which was stretching wrath, can securely sin under the kindness of the grace of God, he subjoined at once: What therefore? Shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? Far be it! Or do you not know that to whom you exhibit yourselves as slaves toward obeying, you are slaves of him whom you have obeyed, whether of sin or of an obedience of justice? Do we already believe him, about whose condition of sin he has discussed until now? To whom, he says, you exhibit yourselves as slaves toward obeying, you are his slaves, whether of sin or of justice. Where here therefore is that sin indicated by the Apostle, which before the times of will, before the pursuit of those obeying, before the age of knowledge and of conscience is invented to have flown over the seeds themselves? Which certainly cannot be found except in the books of the Manichaeans.

lemmas.lexica: LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: But this gave occasion for the same question he had explained above: someone might object that people freed from the law, which threatened wrath, could safely sin under the kindness of God’s grace. He therefore immediately added: ‘What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? Far from it! Or do you not know that when you present yourselves as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one you obey, whether of sin or of obedience to righteousness?’ (Romans 6:15–16). Do we now believe him about the kind of sin he has been discussing? When you present yourselves, he says, as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of that one, whether of sin or righteousness. Where, then, does the apostle indicate here that sin which is imagined to have flown over the very seed before the time of willing, before the activity of obedience, before the age of knowledge and conscience? Such a thing certainly can be found only in Manichaean books.

choices.why: Bodily seed of generation; Julian denies it carries a will's sin.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
